aboutAuthor: Rupal J. Bhansali is Chief Investment Officer and portfolio manager for international and global equities at Ariel Investments. She has spent three decades managing emerging and developed portfolios, and is known for a research-driven, non-consensus style that bridges India training and global mandates.

points.heading: 'And' not 'Or'
points.body: Bhansali rejects false trade-offs imposed by style boxes: a business can be both defensive and growing, a security both bond-like and equity-like. An and checklist and pay-off convexity diagrams keep portfolios across economics, not labels.

points.heading: Capacity-agnostic, compensation-focused
points.body: Stocks or bonds is answered by where on the capital stack you are best compensated after adjusting for real yield, spreads, and currency. Rotation arrows from debt to equity in the same issuer illustrate opportunistic migration.

points.heading: Stand alone with system
points.body: Non-consensus requires a solitude infrastructure, filtered information funnel, field truck counts, and tracking error tolerance, so loneliness is validated by data before payoff.

points.heading: Hunt upset victories
points.body: Treat severe mispricing as tournament upsets where favorites pay little and upsets pay heavily. Governance discount scatter and sanctions timelines show odds mispriced, and option-like payoffs with many small bets manage low hit rate.

points.heading: Ditch the database
points.body: Standardized, lagged screens enforce consensus. Mosaic tiles from factory robots, distribution networks, and hiring patterns build a forward search engine that sees automation doubling ROE before the database does.

points.heading: Do no harm and define a North Star
points.body: A Hippocratic no-go zone for opaque leverage and a north star card that makes no easier than yes keep the hunt coherent. Margin of safety is balance sheet plus business plus price, and patience is the premium for boring compounders.

insights: The and bridge Venn that says great companies are both growth and defensive, not either.
Database versus search engine: Korean factory robots that double future ROE while the screen still shows low historical quality.
The north star card constellation that forces any position to be visible from protect capital, respect risk, and be curious.
conclusion: Non-Consensus Investing argues that being right when everyone else is wrong is not contrarian theater but a disciplined hunt for mispriced assumptions, engineered through and thinking, mosaic research, upset sizing, and a north star that makes discipline feel like identity.
